title: Decisive Independent Out-of-Sample Evaluation of Terminal Torque and Dynamic Predictors on Plantar Flexion and Resistance Recovery

features: terminal set volume (Norbury Set 4 reps * load)
total volume (Norbury sum of reps * load)
prespecified_hypotheses.utility_threshold: DeltaMAE >= 1.0 Nm (or N) with 95% bootstrap CI strictly excluding zero (p < 0.05)

evangelidis_source_model.source_cohort: Evangelidis et al. 2023 (SRC-0115, PMC10030419, N=9 men, 27 obs, hamstrings)
evangelidis_source_model.protocol: 3 blocks of 33 MVCs (99 total fatiguing contractions) across CON, ECC, ISO

direct_transfer_evaluation.source_cohort: Evangelidis et al. 2023 (SRC-0115, PMC10030419, N=9 men, 27 obs, hamstrings)
direct_transfer_evaluation.target_cohort: Križaj et al. 2025 (SRC-0112, Zenodo 15679911, N=21 adults, 42 bilateral obs, plantar flexors)

protocol_comparison.evangelidis: 99 maximal contractions across 3 blocks; severe fatigue (mean retention 72.36%, drop -27.6%) in hamstrings
protocol_comparison.krizaj: 3 brief submaximal contractions; negligible fatigue (mean retention 97.32%, drop -2.68%) in plantar flexors
protocol_comparison.cross_muscle_transfer: Hamstrings (knee flexors) vs Plantar flexors (triceps surae)

direct_transfer_evaluation.transfer_verdict: CATASTROPHIC_TRANSFER_FAILURE: When transferred to Križaj, the fixed Evangelidis tau_end model produces an MAE of 72.50 Nm (bias +72.50 Nm), which is substantially worse than the fixed Evangelidis retention baseline (MAE = 44.97 Nm). Uncalibrated cross-study dynamic torque models cannot generalize across divergent fatigue regimes.

krizaj_evaluation.condition_permutation_invariance: Permuting condition order within participant preserves baseline PreAlone error identically at 10.60 Nm (10.6032 Nm) because the set of 42 bilateral pre/post torque pairs is invariant.

norbury_evaluation.citation: Norbury et al., 2024, Exp Physiol 109: 1335-1348, DOI 10.1113/EP091705
norbury_evaluation.protocol: 4 sets of unilateral leg press to failure at 30% 1RM (LL) and 70% 1RM (HL) in 12 men
norbury_evaluation.discrepancy_resolution: The previous report indicated that adding terminal set volume worsened error from 76.99 N to 84.24 N. Audit revealed an indexing misalignment between condition-sorted actual values and participant-sorted predictions. With strict participant alignment, adding terminal set volume yields MAE = 47.58 N vs 49.50 N at 5 min, and 32.94 N vs 34.38 N at 45 min. However, both 95% CIs cross zero ([-6.13, 10.31] N and [-4.22, 6.87] N), confirming that volume offers no statistically significant predictive gain beyond baseline force alone.

master_conclusion: Decisive independent out-of-sample evaluation confirms that neither dynamic torque parameters (tau_end) nor mechanical exercise volume (load * reps) provide statistically valid predictive signal for post-exercise residual force in humans. 1. Fixed transfer of the Evangelidis model onto Križaj fails catastrophically (MAE = 72.51 Nm vs fixed baseline 44.97 Nm),    driven by divergent fatigue regimes (72% retention over 99 contractions vs 97% retention over 3 contractions). 2. Retraining on Križaj under LOSO yields a baseline PreAlone MAE of 10.60 Nm; adding terminal torque worsens error    to 10.71 Nm (Rule 2) or 10.79 Nm (Rule 1), spanning 10.59-10.79 Nm across all justified matching rules (all 95% CIs cross zero). 3. In Norbury et al. 2024, adding terminal set volume yields non-significant nominal gains (+1.93 N at 5 min, +1.44 N at 45 min;    both 95% CIs cross zero). Thus, bioenergetic mechanical work cannot empirically bridge the strength-endurance boundary in Architecture A.
